See Leuit. 23, 34.}}∷ Scenopégia, vvas at hand. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=3}} And his brethrē {{ls}}aid to him, Pa{{ls}}{{ls}}e from hence, and goe into Ievvrie: that thy Di{{ls}}ciples al{{ls}}o may {{ls}}ee thy vvorkes vvhich thou doe{{ls}}t. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=4}} For no man doeth any thing in {{ls}}ecrete, and {{ls}}eeketh him {{ls}}elf to be in publike. If thou doe the{{ls}}e things, manife{{ls}}t thy {{ls}}elf to the vvorld. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=5}} For neither did his brethren beleeue in him. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=6}} {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore {{ls}}aith to them, My time is not yet come: but your time is alvvaies readie. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=7}} The vvorld can not hate you. but me it hateth: becau{{ls}}e I giue te{{ls}}timonie of it, that the vvorkes there of are euil. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=8}} Goe you vp to this fe{{ls}}tiual day: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`I vvil not yet goe vp''}}`I goe not vp' to this fe{{ls}}tiual day: becau{{ls}}e my time is not yet accompli{{ls}}hed.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=9}} When he had {{ls}}aid the{{ls}}e things, him {{ls}}elf taried in Galilee. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=10}} But after his brethren vvere gone vp, then he al{{ls}}o vvent vp to the fe{{ls}}tiual day, not openly, but as it vvere in {{ls}}ecrete. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=11}} The Ievves therfore {{ls}}ought him in the fe{{ls}}tiual day, and {{ls}}aid, VVhere is he? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=12}} And there vvas much murmuring in the multitude of him. For certaine {{ls}}aid, That he is good. And others {{ls}}aid, No, but he {{ls}}educeth the multitudes. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=13}} Yet no man {{ls}}pake openly of him for feare of the Iewes.⊣
